items.title: GSTN: e-way bill numbers to go from 12 to 14 digits from 1 Jan 2027 (consolidated EWB 10 to 11)
items.body: GSTN advisory dated 4 November 2026 says e-way bill numbers will change from 12 to 14 digits and consolidated e-way bill numbers from 10 to 11 digits, proposed with effect from 1 January 2027, as existing numbering capacity is expected to run out. The new formats will first be released in the sandbox for testing; businesses, ERP/software providers and API users should update their systems, databases and validations before 1 January 2027.

items.title: No TDS on dividends between IFSC aircraft-leasing units if Form 1(N) is given (Notification 141/2026)
items.body: CBDT Notification No. 141/2026 dated 4 November 2026, issued under section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, provides that no tax is deducted on dividend paid by an IFSC unit engaged in aircraft leasing to a company that is also such an IFSC unit, once the recipient furnishes a statement-cum-declaration in Form No. 1(N) for the tax year. The payer must still report these payments in its TDS statement. The notification applies from 1 April 2026.

sources.name: Income Tax Department e-filing portal – Latest News (official)

items.title: RBI eases service export/import reporting: deemed EDF for individuals, ₹10 lakh threshold for others
items.body: The FEMA (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026 (FEMA 23(R)/(2)/2026-RB), applicable from 1 October 2026, treat the EDF as submitted when a resident individual service exporter gives the bank the payment details; other service exporters get this only where the inward remittance is up to ₹10 lakh. For service imports, IDPMS reporting by the bank (within five working days) now applies only to importers other than resident individuals where the invoice/contract value exceeds ₹10 lakh.

items.title: GSTN opens Rule 14B registration for online sellers using e-commerce warehouses; ₹2.5 lakh monthly tax cap
items.body: A GSTN advisory dated 1 November 2026, implementing Rule 14B inserted by Notification No. 05/2026-Central Tax (26 October 2026), lets suppliers selling through TCS-collecting e-commerce operators register in a State where they have no physical presence, using the operator's warehouse as place of business, if they hold a regular GSTIN in another State under the same PAN and monthly output tax on supplies to registered persons does not exceed ₹2.5 lakh. The operator must consent within 7 working days and Aadhaar authentication/document verification must be completed within 15 days of submitting Part B of REG-01. The application is deemed approved on completion of the field visit or 30 days from ARN, whichever is earlier.

items.title: GSTN: dealers in used cooking oil, plastic, tyre & e-waste scrap to take GST TDS registration in REG-07
items.body: A GSTN advisory dated 1 November 2026, following Notification No. 07/2026-Central Tax (27 October 2026), says GST TDS under section 51 now also covers used cooking oil (heading 1518), plastic waste and scrap (3915), tyre waste and scrap (4004) and electrical/electronic waste and scrap (8549), in addition to metal scrap (Chapters 72–81). Persons dealing in these goods must apply for TDS registration in FORM GST REG-07, selecting 'Others' under Constitution of Business in Part B of Table 2 and entering their category.

items.title: GST registration form REG-01 revised: separate OPC category, up to 10 bank accounts, DIN for LLP partners
items.body: A GSTN advisory dated 1 November 2026, following Notification No. 05/2026-Central Tax and Circular No. 257/03/2026-GST (both 26 October 2026), says FORM GST REG-01 has been revised on the GST portal. One Person Company is now a separate constitution with supporting documents, SEZ units/developers must give an SEZ Entity ID, LLPs must give each designated partner's DIN, and up to 10 bank accounts can be reported (if not available, within 30 days of the REG-06 certificate). CIN, FCRN, LLPIN and FLLPIN are validated online and the ARN is generated only after successful validation.

sources.name: ICAI GST & Indirect Taxes Committee – GSTN advisory list (official)

items.title: GST portal adds composition category for persons eligible under section 10(2A); change it via REG-14
items.body: A GSTN advisory dated 1 November 2026 on composition levy functionality adds a new category, 'Person eligible for composition levy under Section 10(2A)', in REG-01, CMP-02, CMP-04 and REG-14. It can be chosen only on its own and not together with the existing section 10(1) categories. Existing composition taxpayers can change their category through an amendment application in REG-14, keeping it consistent across all GSTINs under the same PAN.

sources.name: ICAI GST & Indirect Taxes Committee – GSTN advisory list (official)

items.title: GST registration amendments (except principal place) now auto-approved; OTP verification within 3 days
items.body: A GSTN advisory dated 1 November 2026, implementing Rule 19 as substituted by Notification No. 05/2026-Central Tax (26 October 2026), says amendments other than the principal place of business – such as legal name, partners/directors/Karta and additional places of business – take effect on submission once online validations (PAN, DIN, CIN) pass. OTP verification of the mobile and email of the primary authorised signatory and one promoter/partner/director must be completed within 3 days of submission, or no ARN is generated. Changes to the principal place of business still go to the proper officer.

items.title: GST cancellation (REG-16) now auto-approved if returns filed and tax liability ≤ ₹2.5 lakh per period
items.body: GSTN advisory of 1 Nov 2026 (under revised Rule 20 of the CGST Rules) says REG-16 cancellation applications are approved electronically once all returns due up to the proposed cancellation date are filed; composition, NRTP, OIDAR and ISD taxpayers qualify without an officer. Regular, casual and SEZ taxpayers are auto-approved if output tax liability is ₹2.5 lakh or less in each tax period; above that, GSTR-10 must be filed within three days, failing which the application goes to the tax officer.

items.title: CBIC Instruction 02/2026: no GST arrests, no SCN below ₹10,000, e-way bill interception curbed
items.body: CBIC Instruction No. 02/2026-GST dated 30 October 2026 directs officers not to carry out further arrests under GST and not to issue show cause notices under sections 73, 74 or 74A where the total tax (CGST, SGST/UTGST, IGST and cess) is below ₹10,000. Vehicles may be intercepted only on specific intelligence authorised by a Joint Commissioner or above, with goods allowed to pass if neither supplier nor recipient is in that officer's jurisdiction (unless no e-way bill or origin/destination document exists). These interim measures apply until the GST laws are amended as recommended by the 57th GST Council.

items.title: CBDT notifies Rule 189A & Form 112A: conditions for merger of registered non-profit organisations
items.body: Notification 139/2026 (G.S.R. 961(E)) dated 30 October 2026 inserts Rule 189A in the Income-tax Rules, 2026, allowing a registered NPO to merge only with another of the same or similar objects; a regularly registered NPO cannot merge with a provisionally registered one. Conditions include a five-year bar on changing the merged organisation's objects, no benefit to related persons and audit of both organisations' books as on the merger date. Intimation in Form 112A must be filed with the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner/Commissioner within one month from the end of the month of the merger.

sources.name: Income Tax e-filing portal – Latest news (official)

items.title: CBIC Circulars 265 & 266 (28 Oct 2026): ITC for used-car dealers, NBFC co-lending taxable, toys, R&D
items.body: CBIC issued Circulars 265/11/2026-GST and 266/12/2026-GST on 28 October 2026 on the 57th GST Council's recommendations. Circular 265 clarifies that under the margin scheme for used vehicles only tax on the second-hand vehicles bought is blocked, so ITC on other inputs and services (spares, repairs, rent, marketing) is allowed; sublimation paper falls under heading 4809 at 18%, and the toy entries cover all toys under heading 9503. Circular 266 clarifies that services by an NBFC to a bank under co-lending are taxable at the contract value, recoveries such as registration, road tax, insurance and FASTag form part of vehicle-leasing supply, and a self-certificate by the head of the institution may suffice for the R&D grant exemption.

items.title: From 1 Nov 2026: RCM on cab/vehicle hire to companies applies unless supplier charges 18% GST (was 12%)
items.body: Notification No. 08/2026-Central Tax (Rate) dated 27 Oct 2026 amends entry 15 of the reverse charge list (Notification 13/2017) for renting of passenger motor vehicles by a non-body-corporate supplier to a body corporate: forward charge now applies only where the supplier charges CGST at 9% (earlier 6%). Notification No. 08/2026-Integrated Tax (Rate) makes the matching change from 12% to 18% IGST. Otherwise the body corporate recipient pays GST under reverse charge. Effective 1 November 2026.

items.title: MCA: cost audit report CRA-4 for FY 2025-26 can be filed till 31 Dec 2026 without additional fees
items.body: MCA General Circular No. 06/2026 dated 27 October 2026 provides that Form CRA-4 (cost audit report in XBRL) for FY 2025-26 filed up to 31 December 2026 will not attract additional fees. Filings after that attract all applicable fees, including additional fees counted from the original due date under Rule 6(6) of the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014.

items.title: From 1 Nov 2026: e-commerce delivery services at 5% without ITC; same-line ITC for 5% hotels & restaurants
items.body: Notification No. 06/2026-Central Tax (Rate) dated 27 October 2026 taxes delivery services supplied through an e-commerce operator by persons not liable to register, and delivery of goods supplied through an e-commerce operator, at 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST) without ITC, from 1 November 2026; postal and courier services stay at 18%. The same notification allows hotel accommodation, restaurant and outdoor catering suppliers paying 5% to take ITC on services bought from the same line of business, capped at 5% where the supplier charged more, and gives an optional 5% rate with restricted ITC for passenger transport and renting of electric vehicles. Notification No. 09/2026-Central Tax (Rate) makes the e-commerce operator liable to pay GST under section 9(5) on such delivery services from the same date.

items.title: TDS returns for Jul–Sep 2026 due 31 Oct 2026 in new Forms 138, 140 and 144
items.body: From tax year 2026-27, TDS statements are filed in Form 138 (salary), Form 140 (resident non-salary) and Form 144 (payments to non-residents), replacing Forms 24Q, 26Q and 27Q. The quarterly due dates are 31 July, 31 October, 31 January and 31 May.

items.title: GST on scrap & used cooking oil from 1 Nov 2026: reverse charge, compulsory registration and GST TDS
items.body: From 1 Nov 2026, registered buyers must pay GST under reverse charge on used cooking oil, plastic waste/scrap, tyre waste/scrap and e-waste bought from unregistered suppliers (Notification 04/2026-Central Tax (Rate), with matching IGST/UTGST notifications). Suppliers of these goods and of metal scrap (Chapters 72–81) lose the registration exemption for reverse-charge-only suppliers (Notification 06/2026-Central Tax), and registered buyers of these goods from registered suppliers must deduct GST TDS under section 51 (Notification 07/2026-Central Tax). All three notifications are dated 27 Oct 2026 and implement the 57th GST Council's recommendations.

items.title: GST from 1 Nov 2026: packaged organic fertilisers & retreaded tractor tyres at 5%, psyllium seeds exempt
items.body: Notification No. 02/2026-Central Tax (Rate) dated 27 October 2026 puts all pre-packaged and labelled animal, vegetable or organic fertilisers (including registered seaweed-extract bio-stimulants) and retreaded tractor tyres (heading 4012) in the 5% slab (2.5% CGST), while other retreaded or used tyres, tyre treads and flaps stay at 18%. Notification No. 03/2026-Central Tax (Rate) exempts psyllium seeds (isabgol, 1211 90 13). Matching IGST and UTGST notifications apply from 1 November 2026, implementing the 57th GST Council's recommendations.

items.title: New GST service exemptions from 1 Nov 2026: toll rights, coffee curing, seed storage; e-commerce GTA now taxable
items.body: Notification No. 07/2026-Central Tax (Rate) dated 27 October 2026 exempts, from 1 November 2026, grant of toll-collection rights by government bodies, curing of coffee for cultivators, storage or warehousing of seeds meant for sowing, Seamen's Provident Fund Organisation services, and seat-share helicopter travel to or from the North-Eastern States, Sikkim and Bagdogra. The GTA exemption no longer applies to transport of goods supplied through an e-commerce operator. Matching IGST and UTGST notifications were issued the same day.

items.title: CGST Rules amended (Notification 05/2026): e-commerce warehouse registration, faster cancellation from 1 Nov 2026
items.body: Notification No. 05/2026-Central Tax dated 26 October 2026 amends the CGST Rules; most changes apply from 1 November 2026, with some from 1 December 2026 and 1 April 2027. From 1 November, new Rule 14B lets a seller with no physical presence in another State register there by declaring an e-commerce operator's warehouse as principal place of business, and a substituted Rule 20 requires voluntary cancellation applications in FORM GST REG-16 within 30 days of the event, with qualifying cases cancelled automatically by the portal. Refund changes include a 10-day limit (down from 15) to acknowledge an application or issue a deficiency memo.

items.title: GST changes from 1 Nov 2026: easier post-sale discounts, 90% provisional refund for inverted duty
items.body: Notification No. 03/2026–Central Tax dated 26 October 2026 brings sections 153 to 155 of the Finance Act, 2026 into force from 1 November 2026. A post-supply discount can be excluded from taxable value if the supplier issues a credit note and the recipient reverses the related ITC, without a pre-supply agreement. Inverted-duty refunds become eligible for 90% provisional refund, and the ₹1,000 minimum no longer applies to refunds on goods exported with payment of tax.

items.title: CBIC issues 8 GST circulars (257–264/2026): ITC on demo vehicles allowed, registration guidelines
items.body: CBIC issued Circulars 257/03/2026-GST to 264/10/2026-GST on 26 October 2026 after the 57th GST Council meeting, covering registration documents and processing, show cause notices and adjudication, and receipt of export proceeds. Circular 262/08/2026-GST withdraws para 4.6 of Circular 231/25/2024-GST, so ITC on demo vehicles is not blocked under section 17(5)(a) for dealers under the dealer-agency model.

items.title: From 1 Jan 2027: e-invoice (IRN) needed for RCM self-invoices and import of services (turnover > ₹5 crore)
items.body: Notification 04/2026-Central Tax amends Notification 13/2020-Central Tax so that, from 1 January 2027, e-invoicing also covers self-invoices for supplies received from unregistered persons under reverse charge and for import of services. It applies to registered persons already under e-invoicing, i.e. aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18; existing exclusions continue.

items.title: MCA extends FY 2025-26 filings: AOC-4 till 31 Dec 2026, MGT-7/7A till 31 Jan 2027
items.body: MCA General Circular No. 05/2026 dated 24 October 2026 allows AOC-4 (all variants) to be filed up to 31 December 2026 and MGT-7 / MGT-7A up to 31 January 2027 without additional fees. The time for holding the AGM is not extended, and filings after the extended dates attract additional fees counted from the original due date.

items.title: RBI moves FEMA compounding for overseas investment, ECB/lending & guarantees to Regional Offices
items.body: By A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 28/2026-27 dated 23 Oct 2026, RBI delegated powers to compound contraventions relating to overseas investment, borrowing and lending, and guarantees to select Regional Offices. Overseas-investment cases go to the Regional Office matching the UIN prefix; borrowing, lending and guarantee cases go to the Regional Office with jurisdiction over the applicant's registered office or domicile. Cases without a UIN, or spanning categories handled by different offices, stay with CEFA, Central Office, Mumbai.

items.title: 57th GST Council recommends removing arrest provisions and cutting general penalty to ₹10,000
items.body: At its 8 October 2026 meeting the GST Council recommended omitting the power of arrest, raising the prosecution threshold to ₹5 crore and reducing the maximum general penalty from ₹25,000 to ₹10,000. Refund of accumulated ITC on input services in inverted-duty cases is proposed for credit availed on or after 1 November 2026. These are recommendations and take effect only when notified.

items.title: RBI raises repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50%; stance now 'calibrated tightening'
items.body: On 7 October 2026 the Monetary Policy Committee raised the policy repo rate to 5.50%; the SDF rate is 5.25% and the MSF rate and Bank Rate 5.75%. Loans linked to the repo rate may cost more from their next reset date.

items.title: AY 2026-27 audit cases: tax audit report by 21 Oct 2026, income tax return by 21 Nov 2026
items.body: On 28 September 2026 CBDT extended the due date for tax audit reports for AY 2026-27 from 30 September to 21 October 2026, and the return due date for audit cases from 31 October to 21 November 2026. The extension does not apply to other taxpayers.
